architecture_drivers.driver: Discovery-before-import is mandatory; no external source writes directly to catalog.
Website and PDF imports are long-running, failure-prone, and must be asynchronous/observable.
AI providers are implementation details behind adapters and capability routing.
Universal Catalog Item needs a base entity plus type-specific attributes to avoid schema fragmentation.
Tenant isolation and AI credential isolation are security-critical.
MVP must remain modular but not microservice-heavy.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use Next.js full-stack monorepo plus separate TypeScript BullMQ worker; do not introduce a separate backend framework.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Simplifies MVP while preserving independent scaling for long-running Playwright/OCR/AI jobs.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use BullMQ/Redis for all long-running tasks, including scraping, OCR, AI enrichment, export generation, sync, retries, and re-enrichment jobs.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Accepted risks require retryable, resumable, observable background jobs.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use UniversalCatalogItem base table plus type-specific JSON attributes and normalized first-class fields.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Mitigates universal item schema risk without premature per-type table explosion.

architecture_decisions.decision: Preserve AI Capability Router plus Provider Adapter architecture as the stable interface for all AI integrations.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Business workflows call AI capabilities and never provider SDKs directly.

architecture_decisions.decision: All catalog writes go through deterministic validation from Discovery Session candidate to Catalog Item.
architecture_decisions.rationale: AI never writes directly to inventory/catalog.

architecture_decisions.decision: Tenant isolation is enforced at application query boundaries and database constraints using tenant_id/workspace_id on tenant-owned records.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Accepted security risk requires explicit tenant boundary.

architecture_decisions.decision: PostgreSQL full-text search is MVP search; external search is deferred.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Avoid unnecessary infrastructure until catalog size proves need.

architecture_decisions.decision: Centralize business logic in shared Domain Services using Route Handler -> Service -> Repository -> Prisma and Worker -> Service -> Repository -> Prisma flows.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Keeps route handlers, server actions, and worker processors thin while sharing business logic across web and worker.

architecture_decisions.decision: Organize implementation as a pnpm monorepo with apps/web, apps/worker, and shared packages: domain, ai, scrapers, shared, validation, types.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Supports shared types and domain logic across the web app and worker without duplicating business rules.

architecture_decisions.decision: Treat scraping and AI enrichment as independent pipelines; persist normalized source records so enrichment can be rerun without re-scraping.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Allows provider swaps, prompt/capability changes, validation improvements, and re-enrichment without repeating fragile scraping work.

pipeline_architecture.re_enrichment_support: Persist normalized source records and import artifacts with version/source hashes so users can rerun enrichment after changing provider, prompt, capability route, or validation rules.

selected_stack.rationale: A Next.js full-stack monorepo with a separate BullMQ worker is the simplest scalable architecture: route handlers and server actions stay thin, all business logic is centralized in shared domain services, workers reuse the same domain services, scraping and AI enrichment remain independent pipelines, and the AI Capability Router/Provider Adapter interface remains stable for all AI integrations.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Too risky for Playwright/OCR/AI jobs; workers must scale and run independently.
Adds a second language while frontend, Playwright, and worker ecosystem remain TypeScript-heavy.

Unnecessary until catalog scale proves PostgreSQL full-text insufficient.

architecture_risks.risk: Playwright jobs may be blocked or rate-limited by vendor anti-bot controls.
architecture_risks.mitigation: Bounded crawling, per-vendor throttles, manual fallback, failure states, and Stage 6 representative tests.

architecture_risks.risk: Tenant isolation bug could expose catalog data or AI credentials across workspaces.
architecture_risks.mitigation: Tenant_id on all tenant tables, service-level authorization guards, integration tests, credential encryption.

architecture_risks.risk: Universal Catalog Item JSON attributes become unqueryable if too much domain data is pushed into unstructured fields.
architecture_risks.mitigation: Keep common searchable fields normalized; reserve JSON attributes for type-specific optional fields.

architecture_risks.risk: Queue observability is insufficient for users to understand import state.
architecture_risks.mitigation: ImportJob and ImportJobEvent entities; user-visible statuses; Sentry/log metrics.

architecture_risks.risk: Cloud AI provider costs vary with extraction volume.
architecture_risks.mitigation: Per-workspace provider credentials, job cost logging, provider routing, local Ollama option.

tradeoffs.cost: requires discipline to avoid tangled modules

assumptions_made.assumption: A TypeScript-first stack is the lowest-risk default because Playwright, frontend, workers, API, AI adapters, and validation can share language/tooling.
Next.js route handlers/server actions are sufficient for MVP API complexity when long-running jobs are delegated to workers.
The Domain Service layer and monorepo package boundaries are sufficient to keep Next.js route handlers and worker processors thin without adding a separate backend framework.
